message.title: U.S. Data Center Power Crunch Poses Greater Risk to Memory and Optical Networking Than Nvidia - BigGo Finance
message.body:
U.S. Data Center Power Crunch Poses Greater Risk to Memory and Optical Networking Than Nvidia
The bottleneck in U.S. artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure is shifting from chip shortages to power shortages. Even if servers are installed in data centers, without electricity they cannot be converted into actual computing capacity—raising concerns that AI supply chain risk may concentrate in specific component categories.
Morgan Stanley, in a report released on the 5th (local time), estimated that U.S. data center developers will face a net power shortfall of approximately 32 gigawatts (GW) by 2028. That represents roughly 34% of required power, and the figure already accounts for additional power procurement measures including on-site generation and fuel cells.
The core insight of the analysis is that power shortages will not affect all AI semiconductor companies equally. Nvidia and Broadcom are relatively safe, while suppliers of peripheral components—ASICs, memory, optical networking, and power management semiconductors—could take a bigger hit.
Diverging Impact Across Chipmakers
Morgan Stanley assessed that the power bottleneck does not yet threaten Nvidia's and Broadcom's 2027 earnings outlooks. The two companies have relatively high visibility into which data centers their semiconductors will actually be deployed in, and they have room to respond to power shortages through regional business expansion and coordination among data center operators, semiconductor companies, and power supply chains.
Product efficiency also makes a difference. Nvidia GPUs can produce more tokens per gigawatt of power, giving them higher deployment priority in power-constrained environments. ASICs, by contrast, have lower output per unit of power and require securing more power resources, making them more sensitive to bottlenecks.
Broadcom's guidance revisions also show that market expectations are converging. In March, the company said AI revenue for fiscal 2027 would "significantly exceed" $100 billion, but by September it had specified the figure at $115 billion. The absolute scale remains large, but the room for further upward revision appears limited.
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and Broadcom CEO Hock Tan have both recently emphasized that power resources have become a harder constraint to coordinate than chips or memory in AI infrastructure deployment.
Inventory Risk in the Component Supply Chain
If power constraints translate into actual deployment delays, customers may postpone product deliveries or cancel orders. Morgan Stanley noted that in this scenario, memory, optical networking, power management, and analog semiconductors face the greatest exposure to inventory disruptions.
These component categories have benefited from AI infrastructure expansion and tightening supply-demand dynamics. However, if final projects are delayed, customers are likely to draw down existing inventory first and then reduce follow-on orders. The implication is that expanded AI investment does not automatically translate into revenue growth for all semiconductor companies.
Oracle's case illustrates this risk concretely. "Project Lighthouse," a 1.3 GW facility under construction in Wisconsin, could see power delivery delayed until October 2028 at the earliest—or spring 2029 in a pessimistic scenario—even after transmission approval procedures resumed. Even if AI servers are already mounted in racks, without electricity they cannot be converted into actual computing capacity or revenue.
Efforts to Expand Power Supply—and Their Limits
Morgan Stanley expects new behind-the-meter gas turbine and engine capacity to reach approximately 19 GW from 2026 through 2028 under its base case. Bloom Energy's fuel cells could contribute about 6 GW, while nuclear power and repurposed cryptocurrency mining facilities are also cited as supplementary options. Yet even combined, all these measures fall short of closing the gap.
Overseas expansion offers only a partial solution. Morgan Stanley lowered its forecast for the U.S. share of global computing capacity from 60% to 55%. Slow approval processes in Europe and geopolitical risks in the Middle East are factors limiting demand relocation.
Labor shortages also act as a structural constraint. According to estimates from the Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS), the U.S. will need more than 140,000 additional skilled technical workers by 2030. The current workforce can only support roughly 10–20 GW of new natural gas capacity per year.
Power demand forecasts continue to be revised upward. Morgan Stanley projects additional power demand of 97 GW by 2028—about 43% higher than its previous estimate of 68 GW. After excluding 21 GW of data centers under construction and 19 GW of available or contractable grid capacity, the shortfall reaches 57 GW.
Drivers of demand growth include upward revisions to chip shipment forecasts and changes in server architecture. The transition from traditional servers with 8 GPUs to rack-scale integrated systems has caused power consumption to surge. Nvidia's next-generation "Vera Rubin" rack power assumptions have risen from 149 kW to 234 kW, while "Rubin Ultra" has increased from 415 kW to 600 kW. These figures include not just GPUs but also memory, networking, power delivery, and liquid cooling.
Efficiency improvements are also unlikely to prevent overall power consumption from rising. Morgan Stanley expects token production per watt to increase roughly 6x and per-chip output to increase roughly 15x between 2025 and 2028. However, the analysis suggests that as unit costs fall, AI usage will expand—driving total power consumption even higher.
Political backlash has also emerged as a variable. The state of Texas suspended new data center permit issuance pending completion of an audit. With midterm elections approaching next month, data centers have become a political flashpoint, prompting Big Tech companies to roll out community support measures.
Goldman Sachs expects the near-term impact of political backlash to be limited, while Morgan Stanley identified labor, power, and political issues as the primary obstacles to data center expansion. In the AI industry, whether chips can be produced is no longer the only constraint—securing power and achieving actual operational status have become the next gate determining order fulfillment speed and supply chain profitability.

TrendForce认为传输速率进入1.6 Tbps时代时，铜缆信号衰减预计将加速数据中心短距离传输转向光互连，包括VCSEL NPO和Micro LED CPO。
candidate.subject_time: 传输速率进入1.6 Tbps时代

Echandia开发了基于锂钛氧化物技术的Core海事电池系统，并已获得为印度在建拖船供货的订单。
Yanmar Power Solutions的GH-FC系列海事氢燃料电池系统获得DNV型式认可。

Hexa Creation的技术路线以面向高电压、高功率应用的原生1200V垂直GaN沟槽MOSFET为核心，并将AI数据中心电力基础设施列为目标应用。
Hexa Creation持有美国一所公立大学相关专利及知识产权的独家许可，以支持其高电压垂直GaN技术平台。
USDA发布REAP规则，要求农户完成能源项目并证明一年能源节省后才能申请资金；新要求定于2026-10-16生效。

Reuters reported that two people familiar with the matter identified Denis Coleman and Ashok Varadhan among possible candidates to replace John Waldron as Goldman Sachs COO if Waldron later becomes CEO; the report said no formal succession process had begun.
